news.title: Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller thinks MLS has gained prestige because of the World Cup
news.lede: In his personal monthly newspaper, Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller spoke about the upcoming MLS season and what he’s been focused on these last few weeks. In it, he included hope that the World Cup and an influx of new star players has helped MLS raise its profile on the global stage. “I’m really burning to be on the pitch for 90 minutes regularly and help my lads with everything I’ve got,” wrote Müller. “We have six games in three weeks.

news.title: Fifa vs Uefa: Inside the standoff over Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: The trenches are now being dug as both Gianni Infantino and the Uefa-led alliance against him set out big positions, with no sign of give either way. But that is just opening the way for bigger powers – and more crises like this, writes Miguel Delaney in his latest Inside Football newsletter. As so many senior football figures were thinking about ways to outmanoeuvre each other in the ongoing Fifa crisis – which one source says looks set to become “a long war of attrition” – the main consequence was, naturally, that everyone just dug in. Positions were becoming more entrenched.

news.title: Ivan Toney assault charge details: England striker’s representative respond as court date is set followin
news.lede: England international Ivan Toney has been charged with assault following an alleged incident at a nightclub in central London. The charge was confirmed by the Metropolitan Police and relates to an incident that reportedly took place on Wardour Street in Soho on December 6, 2025. The 30-year-old is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24. Toney, who currently plays for Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, recently returned from the FIFA World Cup, where he represented England under head coach Thomas Tuchel.

news.title: Uefa boycott: England's Lucy Bronze backs decision to potentially miss World Cup
news.lede: Lucy Bronze is a two-time European champion with England. England defender Lucy Bronze says a Uefa boycott of Fifa competitions would be the "right thing" for the future of the game, despite the impact it could have on women's football. After Fifa president Gianni Infantino announced a plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors, European football's 55 member associations voted to boycott all Fifa competitions until the proposals were dropped. The plans have since been aborted - with Infantino apologising for his "errors" - but in a statement on Thursday, Uefa said the boycott could still go ahead.

news.title: Wenger breaks silence on Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA’s chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says Gianni Infantino’s decision to withdraw from a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Tuesday morning a week on from the first reports emerging about Infantino’s plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and sell a 20 per cent stake in it to private equity.

news.title: Argentina FA backs Gianni Infantino after FIFA abandons $20bn World Cup proposal
news.lede: The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has thrown its full support behind under-fire president Gianni Infantino amid an ongoing governance crisis. The massive endorsement arrives shortly after the FIFA boss was forced to abandon a highly controversial $20 billion proposal to sell off commercial rights to the World Cup. AFA has publicly thrown its full weight behind embattled FIFA president Infantino. The backing arrives during a period of intense scrutiny surrounding the world football governing body.
